stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Excavators at a hillside settlement in Anatolia found two kinds of evidence that the village once traded with distant regions. First, they recovered glass beads made in workshops hundreds of miles away. ______ they uncovered bronze weights matching a measuring standard used in faraway coastal markets.
explanation: The first sentence says there are 'two kinds of evidence.' The beads are the first kind, and the weights are the second, separate kind. Both point toward trade, so sentence two adds a new item that points the same way. That calls for an addition word like 'In addition.' This is the basic move behind every addition-and-emphasis transition question: check that the second sentence agrees with the first, then see whether it adds a new item or repeats the same one. Here it adds a new item.

A.why: You reacted to the change of object, from glass beads to bronze weights, and read it as a contrast. A different item is not a disagreement. Both finds support the same claim about trade. Try putting 'and also' between the sentences: it fits, so this is addition.

C.why: You treated the weights as a result of the beads. Finding beads did not cause the weights to exist or be found. They are two independent pieces of evidence for the same conclusion, so a cause-and-effect word doesn't fit.

D.why: 'Instead' means the second thing replaces the first. The excavators did not find weights in place of beads. They found both. The passage even promised 'two kinds,' so nothing is being replaced.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A physiotherapist designed a new warm-up routine for a youth soccer league. The routine was short, lasting only eight minutes, but it proved highly effective. ______, players who used it had half as many hamstring injuries over a season as players who kept the old twenty-minute routine.
explanation: The sentence before the blank claims that the routine 'proved highly effective.' The sentence after it backs that claim up with a striking result: half as many injuries. Sentence two doesn't add a new, separate point. It confirms and strengthens the same point, so 'Indeed' is the right word. You'll use this skill on addition-and-emphasis questions whenever you have to tell 'indeed' (reinforcing a point) apart from a contrast word.

B.why: This is the trap. You saw a surface contrast, eight minutes against twenty, and the word 'but' earlier in the passage, so you reached for a contrast word. The injury result doesn't turn against the claim that the routine was effective. It proves that claim. 'Nevertheless' needs a real reversal, and there isn't one here.

C.why: 'Instead' signals that one option replaces another. The injury result doesn't replace the claim of effectiveness. It is the evidence for it, so the two sentences point the same way.

D.why: 'Otherwise' means 'if not' and introduces what would happen in the opposite case. The sentence describes what actually happened to players who used the routine, not what would have happened if they hadn't.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: An earthquake early-warning network can protect a city in two separate ways once it detects the first, weaker waves of a quake. It sends alerts to residents' phones seconds before strong shaking arrives. ______, it automatically signals trains to brake so that they are moving slowly when the shaking hits.
explanation: The first sentence names a category, 'two separate ways.' Then the passage gives the first way (phone alerts) and the second way (slowing trains). The second sentence adds a parallel item of the same kind, so 'Additionally' fits. When a passage says how many items it has ('two ways,' 'several roles'), expect an addition word before the next item. That is one of the most common setups on addition-and-emphasis questions.

A.why: You assumed the trains brake because the phone alerts went out. Both actions come from the network detecting the first waves. Neither one causes the other. They are two parallel responses, which makes this addition, not cause and effect.

B.why: 'Conversely' introduces the opposite of what came before. Slowing trains isn't the opposite of alerting residents. Both protect the city in the same way the first sentence promised.

D.why: 'Nonetheless' means 'in spite of that,' but the second sentence doesn't go against the first. Nothing about the phone alerts would make you expect the trains not to be slowed, so there's no tension for 'nonetheless' to overcome.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Infants begin tuning in to the sounds of their first language remarkably early. ______, by ten months of age, many babies have already stopped noticing sound differences that their language does not use, even though they could hear those differences at birth.
explanation: The first sentence claims that infants tune in to their language 'remarkably early.' The second sentence gives a vivid fact that confirms it: by ten months, babies have already narrowed their hearing to the sounds their language uses. Sentence two strengthens the same claim rather than adding a separate one, so 'Indeed' is correct. This is the reinforcement half of addition-and-emphasis questions. You'll need it whenever a sentence backs up a claim with sharper evidence.

A.why: This is the trap. 'Stopped noticing' sounds like losing an ability, so it seems to clash with 'tuning in.' But no longer noticing sounds their language doesn't use is exactly what tuning in to that language means. The sentence confirms the claim instead of contradicting it, so a contrast word is wrong.

B.why: 'Otherwise' describes what would happen if the first statement weren't true. The second sentence doesn't describe infants who fail to tune in. It describes what tuning in looks like.

C.why: 'Meanwhile' marks something happening at the same time, often somewhere else. The second sentence isn't a separate event that happens alongside the first. It is evidence for the first sentence's claim.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Fossil pollen grains are valuable to paleobotanists for two reasons. First, each grain is wrapped in a tough outer wall that resists decay, so pollen often survives in rock layers where leaves and wood have long since rotted away. ______ every plant group produces pollen with its own distinctive shape, which lets researchers name the plants that once grew at a site even when no other part of them remains.
explanation: The first sentence says there are two reasons. The sentence after 'First' gives one of them: pollen survives decay. The sentence after the blank gives the second: pollen shapes identify plants. That is a new, separate item of the same kind, and it agrees with the point before it. When a sentence adds another parallel point, you need an addition word, so 'Additionally' is correct. You can test it by putting 'and also' between the two sentences, and it reads naturally. You'll use this skill on real SAT transition questions where a passage lists several roles, uses or achievements, and the blank introduces the next one.

B.why: You probably reacted to the contrast inside the sentence: pollen survives, but 'no other part' of the plant remains. That contrast sits within one sentence. It isn't a disagreement between the two reasons. The second reason doesn't contradict the first. It is the next item on the same list, so a contrast word like 'However' is wrong.

C.why: 'Therefore' says the second sentence happens because of the first. But pollen grains don't have distinctive shapes because their walls resist decay. These are two independent facts, not a cause and its effect.

D.why: 'For instance' introduces a sample of the idea just stated. The distinctive shapes aren't an example of decay-resistant walls. They are a second, separate reason. The passage counts the reasons ('two reasons', 'First'), which tells you the blank opens the next item on the list, not an illustration of the previous one.
